lines.text: David blesses the LORD, his Rock, who trains his hands for war and is his shield and refuge.
David asks why the LORD regards man, and says man is like a breath with days like a passing shadow.
David asks the LORD to part the heavens, make the hills smoke, and rescue him from the deep waters.
David will sing a new song on a harp of ten strings to the One who frees him from the deadly sword.
David pictures sons like plants, daughters like pillars adorning a temple, full storehouses, and no breach in the walls.
